exemption.reason:
These bytes are the first mapping of trial 12's slice with one entry added after it: `round-down`, in scope, for the p. 5 sidebar this mapping had to leave out and its inventory had to reject, because until 0066 no citation this grammar can write identified the earlier of two identical printings (#436). The rejection is gone with it. Nothing else moved. The exemption is unchanged in kind and in reason: no second reading has been run, and adding an entry to a mapping nobody reviewed leaves it a mapping nobody reviewed. An eighth thing for a second reading, then: whether `round-down` belongs in this slice at all, and whether the entries that divide should depend on it -- nothing in pp. 5-12 divides, and what rests on it is printed on pp. 16-17 and in the combat map, which is the cross-map dependency this contract cannot yet express.

Not reviewed, and deliberately so: this is the first mapping of trial 12's slice, written as the mapping step of #433, and no second reading has been run. Recording anything else would claim a review the trial has not. `legacy` is the wrong word and is used for the reason examples/frcp-6-12-81/review.json and examples/hazmat-172-table/review.json already record: it is the only exemption kind that names a tracking issue, and `non-semantic` needs a reviewed map to depart from, which a first mapping does not have. The map is trial evidence and is used for nothing downstream -- there is no map-package.json, nothing packs it, and no engine consumes it. A second reading should look hardest at six things this mapping's own report names as unsettled. Whether the four tables held as one entry each -- skills-table's eighteen rows, actions-table's twelve, ability-modifier-table's sixteen bands and proficiency-bonus-table's eight -- are one rule or many, which this grammar cannot express either way (#433 H1). Whether the three entries split by an extraction artefact are faithfully two entries each: advantage-disadvantage with advantage-granted-by-gm, skill-proficiency-bonus with skill-proficiency-absent, and in each case one sentence of the corpus is divided between them with nothing in the map saying so. Whether the eleven declined entries decline advice or drop rules -- the social interaction and roleplaying sections are nearly two full pages of guidance, and four of the eleven are tables of examples. Whether the four `ambiguity.fate: unresolved` entries are the right four, at 5% of 80 in-scope entries against 1% to 27% across the committed maps -- and, the other side of the same question, whether the eight assertions are rightly assertions: heroic-inspiration-award, check-difficulty-class and improvised-actions each record a judgement the corpus gives a person, and each could have been an ambiguity instead. Whether the 138 term-pointer crossReferences, which were generated from the same detector that obliges them, are each a pointer the corpus makes -- the mapper's judgement went into which terms the vocabulary holds, not into the 138. And whether leaving Attack, Dodge and Influence out of that vocabulary is the right trade (#422).
